items.text: Among peripheral intravenous catheters inserted on adult medical and surgical wards, is insertion in the 12 months after the change to clinically indicated replacement, compared with the 12 months before, associated with a higher proportion of catheter failure?
items.population: Peripheral intravenous catheters inserted on adult medical and surgical wards from 1 March 2024 to 28 February 2026
items.comparator: Insertion in the 12 months before the change
items.outcome: Catheter failure: removal for phlebitis, infiltration, occlusion or dislodgement before the end of treatment
items.setting: 520-bed teaching hospital, adult medical and surgical wards

items.text: Did the number of peripheral catheters per admission fall after the policy change?
items.population: Admissions to the same wards in the same two years
items.comparator: Admission in the 12 months before the change
items.outcome: Number of peripheral catheters inserted per admission

finer: Feasible from existing records within the agreed informatics time; interesting to the executive, ward nurses and infection prevention; novel locally; ethical under the approved waiver of consent; relevant because the policy may be reversed.
summary: One primary PECO question on failure and one secondary question on insertions per admission.
